============================== PAGE 1 ==============================
APPLYING NASA-STD-7009 STANDARD FOR MODELS AND SIMULATIONS TO
SURROGATE AND OTHER STATISTICAL MODELS
K.L. Johnson
NASA Engineering and Safety Center (NESC)
Marshall Space Flight Center, AL
ABSTRACT
NASA-STD-7009A, Standard for Models and Simulations, contains a worthy and
insightfully-crafted credibility assessment. That set of metrics is intended to accumulate and
communicate information that can be critical for users and their customers in evaluating findings
due to a model or simulation. Was the model designed for the present use? Is it validated in the
domain it’s being applied to? And so on.
The Standard was originally focused on physics-based models, but it can be applied
more generally. It can – and should – be applied to high-impact statistical models, including
surrogate models based on larger models and sims and regression models based directly on
data. A key issue with many of such models is their relative simplicity compared to most M&S
despite their use in high risk engineering decisions. This report will make a case for using this
Standard for a wider class of models, and how it might actually add value in excess of its cost for
not only stakeholders, but modelers themselves. A rough example showing compliance for a
statistical model is included.
INTRODUCTION
Excellent mangers depend on excellent information provided by subject matter experts
(SMEs). Information provided by an excellent team of SMEs should enable a manager to make a
decision without having to perform their own investigations or analyses or even be an SME in all
relevant topics themselves.
This, however, does not relieve a manager of the responsibility to weigh the quality of the
inputs. The information that aerospace and defense engineering managers depend on can have
extremely high impact. But the time, resources and even capacity required to fully understand
each input is often simply out of reach. The manager must often rely on snippets of sometimes-
imperfect substantiation offered in many forms and languages.
At the same time, responsible SMEs want their inputs to incur the proper amount of
respect and understanding. Not too little: no competent SME wants a valuable input to be
ignored. Yet not too much: a well-founded fear is that a good but still somewhat uncertain
estimate can “grow legs” and be treated as sure or that a firm recommendation becomes
associated with a condition for which it is invalid.
In short, managers want to and need to know what to believe and how much. SMEs want
to and need to offer inputs attached with the right strength of certainty behind them. And
everyone needs to perform this transaction completely, understandably and succinctly no matter
what the subject matter being communicated.
NASA-STD-7009A Standard for Models and Simulations (to be called here the Standard
or 7009A) [1] was instituted in large part to address these issues for the modeling and simulation
(M&S) community. Acceptance has been sure but slow. The slowness may be in part because it
may seem like “just another set of requirements” that just add complexity and cost.
============================== PAGE 2 ==============================
The Standard’s authors and contributors (including this writer) understand this, but mostly
succeeded in creating a document and process that achieve the Standard’s goals but with little
overhead. While application does take some planning and time, applied judiciously 7009A should
add value in excess of burden. Particularly for high-importance, high-risk models, the structural
requirements within 7009A represents an excellent framework for constructing and exercising
M&S, while the requirements pertaining to documentation and communication help M&S
stakeholders, including future users of the M&S, understand what it is they have in their hands.
The Standard’s credibility scale, in particular, is a succinct and flexible me

lacking, decisional risk may be increased unknowingly and unnecessarily.
To address this set of problems, 7009A begins by outlining and encouraging foundational
best practices. It “establishes uniform practices in M&S to ensure essential requirements are
applied to their design, development and use, while ensuring acceptance criteria are defined by
the P/P and approved by the responsible Technical Authority (TA), … provides an approved set
of requirements, recommendations, and criteria with which M&S may be developed, accepted,
and used in support of NASA activities (and) provides a basic set of best practices applicable to
any M&S.” [1]
7009A is required only in particular circumstances. Specifically, the P/P must include it in
its list of required applicable standards. The P/P TA defines a threshold of risk or criticality over
which an M&S must employ the Standard and its requirements, so only a subset of models will
require adherence.
7009A is comprehensive, covering the life span of an M&S. “This NASA Technical
Standard (establishes) a minimum set of requirements for the key elements related to M&S,
including development, maintenance, operation, results analysis, training, credibility assessment,
and reporting.” A life cycle-based worksheet is included with the Standard (Table 22, also
executed as an Excel worksheet) to help make this clear. A logical story about the particular
model’s generation process is written as a result.
============================== PAGE 4 ==============================
7009A tries hard not to be overly prescriptive. It specifically encourages the TA to tailor
the Standard from the initial stages of P/P planning onward. (Because of this intention, all
examples and recommendations listed in this paper are provisional to P/P tailoring.) 7009A
“covers what needs to be accomplished and communicated, not how it is to be done. Discipline-
specific recommended practice guides should be consulted for specific applications or
methodologies.” This phrasing not only encourages expertise and promotes use of established,
proven methods, it also discourages shortcuts and works to expose inexpert practice.
“In the development of NASA-STD-7009A, the decision was to focus on the product of
models and simulations, rather than on the process of modeling and simulating.” This gives
tremendous freedom to the modeler. What it means, though, is that whatever process is chosen,
the modeler be responsible for communicating how well the model does its job. The Standard is
all about what was accomplished vs not accomplished in terms of answering the question it was
designed to answer. It correctly puts focus on solving the problem rather than on making a model.
This is freeing, as there are often many ways to answer a question well.
WHAT IF 7009A ISN’T REQUIRED – WHY SHOULD I USE IT?
7009A can look hard to apply. Particularly for new users, the Standard can look daunting
and the Handbook detailing its application is thick. Following it does require additional overhead
in planning and documentation over on-the-fly work. Many modelers might prefer to ignore it
away. The Standard’s authors understood this, hence the only requirement to application is that it
be applied to M&S affecting design, verification, risk assessment and similar decisions involving
high risk. There is a case, however, for working to its intent using its basic structure for M&S
involved with lesser risk as well. It doesn’t have to be difficult to use, and statistical modelers are
likely to already be familiar with and already use the structure the Standard asks for. The key is in
understanding, planning and appropriate brevity.

"""Protocol-check — mechanical conformance checks for a reference encoding.

These are the scriptable subset of `docs/Encoding_Protocol_v0_1_DRAFT.md`, seeded by
finding F-6c of the Johnson pilot. They exist so that no workbook reaches the author's
review pass while it still fails a check a machine could have run.

## Why a flag and not a command

The checks have no state of their own and nothing to orchestrate. They are assertions
about an artifact that `extract` has just written or that `import` has just been handed,
so they ride those commands rather than adding a third that would need to be told where
to look.

## Why the two commands behave differently

Every check here describes a *reviewed* workbook. A freshly extracted one has no citation
anchors, because anchors are what the review pass produces, so on `extract` the flag
prints the table and leaves the exit code alone: it is telling the encoder what review has
to produce, not failing them for not having done it yet. On `import` the workbook is the
reviewed one and the checks are gates, so any failure exits non-zero.

## Placeholder detection is pack-derived, not hardcoded

Every pack template carries a description row under each header row, and its strings are
exactly the hint text that leaks into data rows when the extractor writes nothing
(F-3d). The placeholder set is read from the active pack's own template rather than listed
here, so a pack that changes its hints does not silently stop being checked.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

from uofa_cli.excel_constants import SHEET_NAMES

ANCHOR_HEADER = "Source Anchor"

# Files the protocol requires beside a package. Names are conventions rather than
# schema, so they are matched case-insensitively against a small candidate set.
AMBIGUITY_LOG_NAMES = ("ambiguity_log.md", "ambiguity-log.md", "ambiguitylog.md")
RUN_LOG_NAMES = ("run_log.md", "run-log.md", "runlog.md")

# Section 3 of the protocol names these as the run log's mandatory pins.
RUN_LOG_FIELDS = ("model", "backend", "site commit", "repo head", "base_uri")

# A run log that labels itself a pilot must not record a signing step, because a pilot
# runs before the protocol governs it and nothing it produces may be signed.
PILOT_MARKERS = ("pilot", "PILOT")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CheckResult:
    """One check, its verdict, and enough detail to act on a failure."""

    name: str
    passed: bool
    detail: str = ""
    skipped: bool = False


def _sheet_header_row(ws, first_header: str) -> int | None:
    for row in range(1, 12):
        for col in range(1, 40):
            value = ws.cell(row=row, column=col).value
            if isinstance(value, str) and value.strip() == first_header:
                return row
    return None


def _anchor_col(ws) -> int | None:
    for col in range(1, 40):
        for row in range(1, 12):
            if ws.cell(row=row, column=col).value == ANCHOR_HEADER:

    return None

}

    """The hint strings a pack's own template puts in its description rows."""

    import openpyxl

def _print_provenance_counts(output: Path) -> None:
    """Per-class field counts. See R5 in docs/valid-package-spec.md."""
    import collections
    import json

    try:
        blob = json.loads(output.read_text())
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return
    node = blob if "fieldProvenance" in blob else next(
        (n for n in (blob.get("@graph") or []) if isinstance(n, dict)
         and "fieldProvenance" in n), None)
    if not node:
        return
    entries = node.get("fieldProvenance") or []
    counts = collections.Counter(e.split("=")[-1] for e in entries
                                 if isinstance(e, str) and "=" in e)
    if not counts:
        return
    parts = ", ".join(f"{n} {cls}" for cls, n in sorted(counts.items()))
    info(f"  field provenance: {parts}")
    if not counts.get("extracted"):
        info("  NOTHING in this package was read from the document — every "
             "field came from the run, a default, or a synthesis.")

def resolve_criteria_set(standards_reference: str, base_uri: str) -> str:
    """Identifier for the rubric an assessment was graded against.

    A recognised published standard is a shared concept, so it gets the stable
    project-controlled identifier under CRITERIA_BASE. Anything else is the
    author's own rubric and is minted in the author's namespace, because the
    project cannot speak for a criteria set it has never seen.

    Aliases are folded so that "ASME V&V 40", "asme-vv40-2018" and
    "ASME_VV40_2018" resolve to one identifier rather than three.
    """
    normalized = re.sub(r"[^A-Z0-9]", "", (standards_reference or "").upper())
    canonical = KNOWN_CRITERIA_SETS.get(normalized)
    if canonical:
        return f"{CRITERIA_BASE}/{canonical}"
    # Org-level, not under the COU: a rubric is shared across an author's
    # assessments, so burying it beneath one context of use would be wrong.
    return f"{base_uri}/criteria/{slugify(standards_reference)}"

_DEFERRED_TO_SIGNING = {"hash", "signature"}


def _profile_requirements(packs: list[str]) -> dict[str, set[str]]:
    """Required property names per profile body, read from the shapes.

    Read, never hardcoded: a copy of the shape's requirements is a copy that
    drifts, and this repository has already moved PROFILE_URIS off a literal
    onto `sh:in` for that reason.
    """
    from rdflib import Graph, Namespace
    from uofa_cli import paths as _paths

    SH = Namespace("http://www.w3.org/ns/shacl#")
    g = Graph()
    for f in _paths.all_shacl_schemas(active=list(packs)):
        try:
            g.parse(f, format="turtle")
        except Exception:
            continue
    out: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
    for name in ("Disposition", "Complete", "Minimal"):
        shape = next((x for x in g.subjects(None, None)
                      if str(x).endswith(f"UnitOfAssurance_{name}Body")), None)
        if shape is None:
            continue
        req, frontier = set(), [shape]
        while frontier:
            n = frontier.pop()
            for prop in g.objects(n, SH.property):
                mc = g.value(prop, SH.minCount)
                if mc is not None and int(mc) >= 1:
                    req.add(str(g.value(prop, SH.path)).split("#")[-1])
            frontier.extend(g.objects(n, SH.node))
        out[name] = req
    return out


def derive_profile(doc: dict, packs: list[str]) -> tuple[str | None, set[str]]:
    """The highest profile the CONTENT satisfies, and what the closest one lacks.

    Every package used to declare whatever the spreadsheet said, which is how all
    five gpt-5 extractions came to claim ProfileComplete without containing
    Complete's fields -- an aspiration the shape then measured as a claim.

    Order is Disposition, Complete, Minimal: Disposition is CompleteBody plus
    hasDisposition via sh:node, so it is strictly the most demanding. Ranking by
    what a shape DEMANDS rather than by what is adopted keeps the order stable.

    Returns (None, missing) when nothing is satisfied, so the caller can fail
    loudly naming the gap rather than declaring a profile the package does not
    meet.
    """
    reqs = _profile_requirements(packs)
    present = {k for k, v in doc.items() if v not in (None, "", [], {})}
    closest, fewest = None, None
    for name in ("Disposition", "Complete", "Minimal"):
        need = reqs.get(name)
        if not need:
            continue
        missing = {r for r in need if r not in present} - _DEFERRED_TO_SIGNING
        if not missing:
            return name, set()
        if fewest is None or len(missing) < len(fewest):
            closest, fewest = name, missing
    return None, (fewest or set())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""A-8 recovery method: predeclared (required) credibility levels from cell shading.

The source states the *achieved* credibility levels in prose (p.25) but states the
*predeclared / required* levels only as green cell fill on its copy of 7009A Table 3
(p.7). There is no text an extractor could read. This script recovers them from the
page's fill geometry so that a second encoder can repeat the recovery exactly.

Method
------
1. Take page 7 (0-indexed page 6) of the source PDF.
2. Collect every filled rectangle whose non-stroking colour is the table's green,
   RGB (0.761, 0.839, 0.608).
3. Keep only the *cell-sized* rectangles: Word emits one rectangle per shaded cell plus
   one per shaded text line inside it, so filter on height >= 40 pt (cell rows on this
   page are 89-116 pt tall; line rectangles are ~9-10 pt).
4. Bucket each surviving rectangle by its column x-range and its row y-range.
5. Name the columns from the header words on the same page (the eight 7009A factor
   headings) and the rows from the level digits printed in the leftmost column.

Run:  python3 shading_recovery.py [path-to-pdf]
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import sys
import pdfplumber

GREEN = (0.761, 0.839, 0.608)
CELL_MIN_HEIGHT = 40.0          # pt — separates cell fills from per-line fills
PAGE_INDEX = 6                  # printed page 7


def recover(pdf_path: str):
    with pdfplumber.open(pdf_path) as pdf:
        page = pdf.pages[PAGE_INDEX]

        cells = [r for r in page.rects
                 if r.get("non_stroking_color") == GREEN
                 and r["height"] >= CELL_MIN_HEIGHT]

        # Column names: the factor headings sit above the table body (top < 158).
        # Each heading is stacked over several lines, so group heading words by the
        # column band their x-midpoint falls into.
        columns = sorted({(round(r["x0"], 1), round(r["x1"], 1)) for r in cells})
        bands: list[tuple[float, float]] = []
        for x0, x1 in columns:
            if not bands or x0 > bands[-1][1] + 1:
                bands.append((x0, x1))

        heads = {b: [] for b in bands}
        for w in page.extract_words():
            if w["top"] >= 158:                     # table body, not the header
                continue
            mid = (w["x0"] + w["x1"]) / 2
            for b in bands:
                if b[0] - 4 <= mid <= b[1] + 4:
                    heads[b].append((round(w["top"], 1), w["text"]))
        names = {b: " ".join(t for _, t in sorted(v)).replace("- ", "")
                 for b, v in heads.items()}

        # Row levels: the digits 1-4 printed in the leftmost (Level) column.
        levels = [(w["text"], w["top"]) for w in page.extract_words()
                  if w["x0"] < 104 and w["text"] in {"1", "2", "3", "4"}
                  and 150 < w["top"] < 620]

        out = []
        for r in sorted(cells, key=lambda r: r["x0"]):
            band = next(b for b in bands if b[0] - 1 <= r["x0"] <= b[0] + 1)
            level = next(lv for lv, top in levels if r["top"] <= top <= r["bottom"])
            out.append((names[band], int(level),
                        (round(r["x0"], 1), round(r["top"], 1),
                         round(r["x1"], 1), round(r["bottom"], 1))))
        return out


if __name__ == "__main__":
    path = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "../source/NTRS-20200002832-Johnson-2020.pdf"
    rows = recover(path)
    print(f"{'7009A Table 3 factor (p.7)':<42} {'required level':>14}   shaded-cell bbox")

        print(f"{name:<42} {level:>14}   {bbox}")
    print(f"\n{len(rows)} shaded cells recovered "

# AMBIGUITY_LOG.md — Johnson (2020), NTRS-20200002832

Created empty at A-1; entries added as they arose, through A-13. Each entry states the
ambiguity, the resolution chosen, and the rule applied in choosing it. Entries marked
**ESCALATION** are not resolutions: they record a gap met and not worked around.

Nothing here harmonises a contradiction silently. Where the source answers a question two ways,
both readings are recorded with an anchor each.

---

## AMB-01 — The source is half evidence and half tutorial, in one voice (A-1)

**Ambiguity.** A rule admitting "the published document" admits both the worked example (the
only evidence about a model in this source) and 12 pages of argument about why NASA-STD-7009A
should be applied to statistical models, written in the same voice and often in the same
paragraph as the worksheet commentary.

**Resolution.** The evidence boundary in `SOURCE_SCOPING.md` §4 admits the worked example, its
Life-Cycle Worksheet, the two credibility tables, the reporting responses and the bibliographic
matter, and excludes the abstract, introduction, the "why use it" argument, the uncertainty-
propagation notes, the conclusions and the acknowledgments. Worksheet commentary paragraphs are
admitted per sentence, only where they state a fact about *this* modelling effort.

**Rule applied.** A-1: draw the boundary before close reading, list admitted and excluded
separately, and let the anchor name the passage rather than the page.

## AMB-02 — The source discloses its own distortion

**Ambiguity.** p.5: "The example is from a real aerospace application highly disguised as a test
of puncture resistance in a multi-ply tire on an experimental aircraft." The encoded subject
matter is therefore known not to be the real subject matter.

**Resolution.** Encode what the source states — tire, FOD particle, aircraft, 0.16 cm critical
depth — and say here that the source describes the case as disguised. No attempt is made to
guess the real application.

**Rule applied.** A-9: "Where the source discloses its own distortion… encode what the source
states and say that you did."

## AMB-03 — The source is written against 7009A; the pack encodes 7009B

**Ambiguity.** The assessment is written against NASA-STD-7009A w/Change 1 (2016) (p.5, p.28
ref [1]). The only NASA pack available is `nasa-7009b` v0.5.0, which encodes NASA-STD-7009**B**
and whose 19-factor list is not the source's 8-factor list. The workbook's Standards Reference
dropdown offers `NASA-STD-7009B` but not `NASA-STD-7009A`.

**Resolution.** The cell records **NASA-STD-7009A**, the standard the source names, not the
dropdown value. The pack version (`nasa-7009b` 0.5.0) and the standard version
(NASA-STD-7009A) are recorded as two separate facts in `RUN_LOG.md` §2. Note that the CLI's
criteria-set resolver maps the version-agnostic aliases `NASA-STD-7009` and `NASA7009` onto the
**B** identifier, so an assessment entered the natural way would be graded against a standard
it does not claim; writing "NASA-STD-7009A" avoids that, resolving instead to a criteria-set
identifier minted in this encoding's own namespace. (At the profile this package earns, the
criteria-set field is not written at all — see AMB-11.)

**Consequence worth flagging to the author.** The importer stamps 13 of the pack's 19 factors
with `factorStandard: "ASME-VV40-2018"`, a third standard the source never mentions. Those 13
rows are all unpopulated here, so nothing is asserted against V&V 40 — but the stamps are in
the package.

**Rule applied.** A-13: record the pack version and the standard version as separate facts.

## AMB-04 / **ESCALATION ESC-1** — The source's factor vocabulary does not map onto the pack's

**Gap.** NASA-STD-7009A Appendix E, as reproduced on p.7 and scored on p.25, has **eight**
factors: Data Pedigree, Verification, Validation, Input Pedigree, Uncertainty Characterization,
Results Robustness, M&S History, M&S Process/Product Management. The pack expects **nineteen**:
13 V&V 40 factors plus 6 NASA-only ones. Only two labels are shared: **Data pedigree** and
**Results robustness**.

- The source's single **Verification** level (required 3, achieved 4) would have to be split
  across five pack factors (software quality assurance, numerical code verification,
  discretization error, numerical solver error, use error). The source gives no per-factor
  level to distribute.
- The source's single **Validation** level (required 1, achieved 1) would have to be split
  across six pack factors.
- **Uncertainty Characterization** (4/4), **M&S History** (3/3) and **M&S Process/Product
  Management** (2/4) resemble the pack's *Results uncertainty*, *Use history* and *Development
  process and product management* but do not share their labels, and the mapping would require
  reading NASA-STD-7009B's factor definitions, which are outside the evidence boundary.
- **Input Pedigree** (3/3) has no pack counterpart at all and is additionally over-determined
  against *Model inputs* — see AMB-08.

**Resolution.** Populate levels only where the pack's factor label **is** the source's factor
label, so the mapping needs no interpretation of either revision's factor definitions:
`Data pedigree` (3/3) and `Results robustness` (4/4). Decline the other six source factors and
populate no level for the other 17 pack factors. The rule is written into each declined row's
rationale so a second encoder can apply the same bright line.

**Consequence, stated per A-10.** The package carries 2 of the source's 8 assessed factors.
Both of the source's **exceedances** — Verification 3→4 and Process/Product Management 2→4,
the two results the worked example exists to demonstrate — fall on declined factors and are
invisible in the package. Any metric derived from levels reads against 2 populated factors and
17 empty ones, against a source that asserts eight. Understating the source is the smaller
failure, but it is not a free one.

**Why an escalation and not a resolution.** The schema cannot express "the source assessed a
factor this pack does not have", and there is no field in which to record an assessed level
against a factor label the pack does not carry. This entry is to be amended, not replaced, if a
7009A pack or a published 7009A→7009B factor concordance later arrives.

## AMB-05 / **ESCALATION ESC-3** — Model risk level has no mechanical source

**Gap.** The workbook requires `Model Risk Level` as "MRL 1–5 per V&V 40 Table 4-1". The source
states the two inputs qualitatively — "high M&S results influence, in the words of the
Standard. The Project also found that the decision held high consequence" (p.11) — together
with a criticality assessment (p.11: single point failure, ~1/300 probability of catastrophic
failure, probable loss of aircraft with significant likelihood of pilot loss). V&V 40 Table 4-1,
which converts influence × consequence onto 1–5, is not in the source and is outside the
evidence boundary.

**Resolution.** Declined; the cell is empty. The extractor's "MRL 3" was corrected out.

**Consequence, stated per A-10.** Three weakener patterns are silenced because they are
conditioned on `modelRiskLevel`: **W-EP-04** (unassessed factor at MRL > 2), **W-NASA-01**
(data pedigree unassessed at MRL > 1) and **W-NASA-04** (use history unassessed at MRL > 2).
Seventeen unassessed factors and a source that describes a potentially fatal failure mode
therefore draw no risk-conditioned firing at all. `modelRiskLevel` is also mandatory for
ProfileComplete, so the declination is one of the reasons the package earns only Minimal
(AMB-11).

**Rule applied.** A-10: decline rather than invent; disclose the declination and its
consequence in the encoding.

## AMB-06 — Contradiction: how many reviewers

**Reading A (p.10, [M&S 36] response):** "Independent reviews performed by three statistical
modelers and more than three engineering practitioners."
**Reading B (p.24, worksheet Technical Review, [M&S 36] row):** "Statistical analysis, model and
findings due to analysis reviewed by **two** NASA statisticians… Test performance, data, model
and findings reviewed by team and independently by engineers."

**Resolution.** Neither reading is preferred. Both are quoted in the description of the
`Independent technical review of analysis, model and findings` evidence row, with this entry
cited. Nothing in the package turns on the count.

**Rule applied.** A-9: record the reading chosen and enter the contradiction with an anchor for
each reading; never harmonize silently. Here the reading chosen is "both, quoted".

## AMB-07 — Contradiction: an approved waiver and no waiver at all

**Reading A (p.6, PREDECLARATIONS ¶3):** "Verification of the analysis code **was waived** since
modeling required relatively straightforward multiple linear regression analysis…"
**Reading B (p.8, [M&S 32](7)):** "Validation using RWS or independent data not required per
investigation team, approved by Technical Authority. **No waivers were required.**" — a single
response that both describes a Technical-Authority-approved dispensation and denies that any
waiver was needed.
**Reading C (p.23, worksheet Caveats, [M&S 32](7) row):** "Waivers to requirements — **None**."

**Resolution.** All three are recorded: A in the rationale of the `Numerical code verification`
factor row, B and C beside it and in the Decision rationale. The package asserts no waiver flag
anywhere, because the field the pack offers for it does not exist and because the source's own
answer is self-contradictory. A-9's tie-break ("the answer outranks the declination") settles
the *validation* half of Reading B — the dispensation described is an answer and "no waivers
were required" is a declination — but it does not settle Reading A against Reading C, both of
which are answers. That residue is **author judgment and remains open.**

**Note on the mechanical check.** The A-7 check that fires when required equals achieved on
every factor is released by a recorded waiver. It is released here by Reading A, quoted in the
row it concerns (`Numerical code verification`, the analysis-code verification that was waived).
That is where the waiver belongs; it was not placed on either populated factor.

## AMB-08 — Over-determination: two source factors point at one pack factor

**Ambiguity.** The pack factor `Model inputs` is answered by two different source factors:
`Input Pedigree` (required 3, achieved 3; p.7, p.25 "Data from controlled test… measurement
system accuracy and precision shown to have inconsequential impact on results") and the input
half of `Validation` (required 1, achieved 1). The source gives no rule for combining them, and
they differ by two levels.

**Resolution.** Declined; no level populated; both source factors named in the row's rationale
and anchor. Folded into ESC-1.

**Rule applied.** A-9 (over-determination) and A-10 (decline rather than invent).

## AMB-09 — The radar figure was not used as a source of numbers

**Ambiguity.** pp. 9–10 carry a star/radar glyph plotting required (blue) against achieved
credibility for all eight factors. It is a second statement of the same values, at figure
precision.

**Resolution.** No value was read off the figure. The figure is used only as a *corroboration*
of the shading recovery: its title, "Credibility Meets or Exceeds Requirements", is inconsistent
with any recovered required level exceeding its achieved level, and none does
(`SHADING_RECOVERY.md`, corroboration 3).

**Rule applied.** A-8: where a value is recoverable only by non-textual means, name the method.
Reading eight polygon vertices off a bitmap glyph is not a method that reproduces, so it was not
used to produce values.

## AMB-10 — Level scales

**Ambiguity.** The source scores on 0–4 ("A lower level 0 indicates insufficient evidence to
make a determination", p.7). The pack uses 0–4 for its six NASA-only factors and 1–5 for its 13
V&V 40 factors.

**Resolution.** Both populated factors (`Data pedigree`, `Results robustness`) are NASA-only
factors on the pack's 0–4 scale, so the levels transfer with no rescaling. No 0–4 value was
ever written onto a 1–5 factor. Residual risk, recorded rather than resolved: identical labels
and identical scales across two revisions of a standard do not guarantee identical *level
descriptors*, and 7009B's descriptors are outside the boundary. The acceptance-criteria cell of
each populated row therefore quotes 7009A's own descriptor text, so a reader can see which
rubric the number was scored against.

## AMB-11 — Profile: left blank, derived, earned

**Ambiguity.** The workbook asks for Minimal or Complete. The source declares no such thing.

**Resolution.** The cell is left empty (source-absent). The importer defaults to Minimal and
then **derives** the profile from package content; the package declares
`ProfileMinimal`, read out of the package rather than off the console. Complete is unreachable
because `modelRiskLevel` was declined (AMB-05) and would also require an assurance level the
source does not state.

**Consequence.** At Minimal the importer does not write `assuranceLevel`, `criteriaSet`,
`deviceClass`, `couName`, `hasUncertaintyQuantification` or the derived credibility metrics.
See AMB-12.

**Rule applied.** A-13: the declared profile must be earned rather than asserted.

## AMB-12 — The source's UQ is quantified but the package does not carry the UofA-level flag

**Ambiguity.** The source gives a quantitative results-uncertainty estimate ([M&S 33](1), p.9:
residual standard deviation 0.0084 cm). The workbook's `Has UQ?` cell records **Yes**, but the
importer writes `hasUncertaintyQuantification` at UofA level only for ProfileComplete, which
this package does not earn (AMB-11).

**Resolution.** The workbook keeps "Yes" (it is what the source says); the package carries the
UQ instead on the evidence node that reports it (`hasUncertaintyQuantification: true`,
`uqMethod`, `metricValue` on the output-comparison result). The UofA-level flag is absent, so
W-AL-02 (UQ present, no sensitivity analysis) cannot fire and W-NASA-05 could not have fired.
A reader who looks only at the UofA node will not see that this source quantifies its
uncertainty.

## AMB-13 — Who the assessor is

**Ambiguity.** K.L. Johnson (NASA NESC) is the author of the published document (p.1 byline).
The modeller inside the worked example is never named: p.24 gives only qualifications ("PhD in
statistics and mathematics… 22 years' experience with NASA").

**Resolution.** `Assessor Name` records Johnson with the role stated ("author of the published
worked example") and the fact that the example's modeller is unnamed. The importer records this
as `statedAssessor` (an extracted fact) and keeps it distinct from `wasAttributedTo`, which is
the operator of this encoding run.

## AMB-14 — The NTRS identifier is not in the document

**Ambiguity.** The document text carries no DOI, report number or URI. "NTRS-20200002832" comes
from the **file name supplied with the task**, not from any admitted passage.

**Resolution.** Recorded, and recorded as such: the workbook anchor for the Source Document cell
says the number comes from the file name. The cell itself holds an IRI minted under this
encoding's namespace (`…/source/ntrs-20200002832-johnson-2020`), because a bare citation string
is dropped from the RDF graph as a non-well-formed subject and the provenance link would then
be invisible. The full citation lives in `SOURCE_SCOPING.md` §1 and in the workbook anchor.

## AMB-15 — Departure from A-3: the documentation-site commit is not pinned

**Gap.** A-3 requires the documentation-site commit current on the day of the run. Outbound
HTTPS to uofa.net returns 403 through this environment's proxy, so no commit could be read.

**Resolution.** Not pinned, and said so in `RUN_LOG.md` §2 rather than left blank or guessed.
A departure from the procedure, recorded here per A-13.

## AMB-16 — Departure from A-3: no repository head to pin

**Gap.** A-3 asks for "your repository or tool version". There is no git checkout in this
environment — the CLI is an installed wheel — so no commit SHA exists to record.

**Resolution.** `uofa-cli 0.11.0` is recorded as the whole of what can be pinned, together with
the pack version and the prompt hash. Recorded as a departure per A-13.

## AMB-17 / **ESCALATION ESC-4** — The importer writes fields the source does not support

**Gap.** Three values appear in the package that no admitted passage supports and that the
workbook offers no way to decline:

1. `reviewType: "internal"` on both ReviewActivity nodes. The source describes these reviews as
   **independent** ("Independent reviews performed by…", p.10; "reviewed by team and
   independently by engineers", p.24). "internal" is an importer default for a SHACL-required
   field.
2. `reviewer: <…/org/reviewer>` on both ReviewActivity nodes — a synthesized IRI, generated
   because the "Compares To" column was correctly left empty (a review activity has no
   comparator).
3. `wasGeneratedBy: <…/activity>` on all five evidence nodes. The importer generates these so
   that W-EP-02 does not fire on every imported result; the source describes no such activity
   entities.

**Why an escalation.** These are assertions in the package's own voice that were not read from
the source and cannot be turned off from the workbook. Working around them (for example by
writing false "Compares To" values to steer the defaults) would be worse. Recorded, not
resolved. Consequence: **W-EP-02 cannot fire on this package**, and its silence must not be read
as the source having documented generation activities for its evidence.

## AMB-18 — Departure from A-2: the minting namespace is not one the encoder controls

**Gap.** A-2 requires a namespace the encoder controls. This encoding was performed by an
automated assistant with no domain of its own, and the author's namespace was not supplied.

**Resolution.** Identifiers are minted under `https://reference-encodings.example.net/uofa`, a
reserved documentation domain (RFC 2606) chosen so it cannot collide with a real namespace.
Because `--base-uri` was passed explicitly, `uofa import` prints no placeholder-domain warning;
that silence does not mean A-2 is satisfied. **Pre-signing blocker:** the package must be
re-imported under a namespace the author controls before it is signed, since the identifier is
covered by the signature and cannot be corrected afterwards.

## AMB-19 — Contradiction: validation both not performed and performed by other means

**Reading A (p.6, PREDECLARATIONS):** "Validation will not be performed." (p.19: "No model
confirmation/ validation using independent data planned or performed.")
**Reading B (p.25, final credibility assessment, Validation row):** "1. No validation runs
planned. RWS data not available. **Validation by visual analysis of test data vs model
expectation.** Problem statement clear; model describes test data well…" — and the factor is
scored 1, not 0, against a predeclared requirement of 1.

**Resolution.** Both recorded; not harmonized. Nothing in the package turns on it, because the
validation-family factors are declined under ESC-1 and carry no level. Reading A is quoted in
the Requirement entity's description; Reading B is quoted in the `Output comparison` row's
rationale.

## AMB-20 / **ESCALATION ESC-2** — No evidence class for a sensitivity analysis

**Gap.** The source documents its sensitivities ([M&S 30], p.22: "Penetration depth is sensitive
to both particle velocity and orientation at impact"; p.25 Results Robustness: "Sensitivities
captured in quantitative model, including for combination of factors (interaction)"). The pack's
evidence-type vocabulary is `ValidationResult | ReviewActivity | ProcessAttestation |
DeploymentRecord | InputPedigreeLink`. There is no SensitivityAnalysis class, and
`hasSensitivityAnalysis` cannot be written from a workbook at all.

**Resolution.** Declined: no evidence node was created for the sensitivity findings, and the
`Results robustness` factor's Linked Evidence cell is empty. Typing them as a ValidationResult
to silence the rule would misdescribe them.

**Consequence.** **W-NASA-06** fires ("Results robustness factor is assessed but has no linked
SensitivityAnalysis evidence") and is dispositioned Accepted: it is true of the package. It is
false of the source, which documents its sensitivities. That difference is this entry.

## AMB-21 — A process attestation the source supports was not created

**Ambiguity.** p.25 rates M&S Process/Product Management 4 on "Standard formal experimental
design and data analysis process rigorously followed and documented in standard form… All review
comments addressed", and p.10 records configuration control and archiving. The pack has a
`ProcessAttestation` evidence class that would fit.

**Resolution.** Not created. The factor it would support is declined under ESC-1, so the
attestation would hang off nothing, and the source describes the process rather than attesting
to it in a form the class expects (`processType`, `attestedBy` are importer defaults — see
ESC-4). Recorded so that the absence is visible as a choice rather than an oversight; a named
reviewer may reverse it.

## AMB-03 — The source is written against 7009A; the pack encodes 7009B

**Ambiguity.** The assessment is written against NASA-STD-7009A w/Change 1 (2016) (p.5, p.28
ref [1]). The only NASA pack available is `nasa-7009b` v0.5.0, which encodes NASA-STD-7009**B**
and whose 19-factor list is not the source's 8-factor list. The workbook's Standards Reference
dropdown offers `NASA-STD-7009B` but not `NASA-STD-7009A`.

**Resolution.** The cell records **NASA-STD-7009A**, the standard the source names, not the
dropdown value. The pack version (`nasa-7009b` 0.5.0) and the standard version
(NASA-STD-7009A) are recorded as two separate facts in `RUN_LOG.md` §2. Note that the CLI's
criteria-set resolver maps the version-agnostic aliases `NASA-STD-7009` and `NASA7009` onto the
**B** identifier, so an assessment entered the natural way would be graded against a standard
it does not claim; writing "NASA-STD-7009A" avoids that, resolving instead to a criteria-set
identifier minted in this encoding's own namespace. (At the profile this package earns, the
criteria-set field is not written at all — see AMB-11.)

**Consequence worth flagging to the author.** The importer stamps 13 of the pack's 19 factors
with `factorStandard: "ASME-VV40-2018"`, a third standard the source never mentions. Those 13
rows are all unpopulated here, so nothing is asserted against V&V 40 — but the stamps are in
the package.

**Rule applied.** A-13: record the pack version and the standard version as separate facts.

## AMB-04 / **ESCALATION ESC-1** — The source's factor vocabulary does not map onto the pack's

**Gap.** NASA-STD-7009A Appendix E, as reproduced on p.7 and scored on p.25, has **eight**
factors: Data Pedigree, Verification, Validation, Input Pedigree, Uncertainty Characterization,
Results Robustness, M&S History, M&S Process/Product Management. The pack expects **nineteen**:
13 V&V 40 factors plus 6 NASA-only ones. Only two labels are shared: **Data pedigree** and
**Results robustness**.

- The source's single **Verification** level (required 3, achieved 4) would have to be split
  across five pack factors (software quality assurance, numerical code verification,
  discretization error, numerical solver error, use error). The source gives no per-factor
  level to distribute.
- The source's single **Validation** level (required 1, achieved 1) would have to be split
  across six pack factors.
- **Uncertainty Characterization** (4/4), **M&S History** (3/3) and **M&S Process/Product
  Management** (2/4) resemble the pack's *Results uncertainty*, *Use history* and *Development
  process and product management* but do not share their labels, and the mapping would require
  reading NASA-STD-7009B's factor definitions, which are outside the evidence boundary.
- **Input Pedigree** (3/3) has no pack counterpart at all and is additionally over-determined
  against *Model inputs* — see AMB-08.

**Resolution.** Populate levels only where the pack's factor label **is** the source's factor
label, so the mapping needs no interpretation of either revision's factor definitions:
`Data pedigree` (3/3) and `Results robustness` (4/4). Decline the other six source factors and
populate no level for the other 17 pack factors. The rule is written into each declined row's
rationale so a second encoder can apply the same bright line.

**Consequence, stated per A-10.** The package carries 2 of the source's 8 assessed factors.
Both of the source's **exceedances** — Verification 3→4 and Process/Product Management 2→4,
the two results the worked example exists to demonstrate — fall on declined factors and are
invisible in the package. Any metric derived from levels reads against 2 populated factors and
17 empty ones, against a source that asserts eight. Understating the source is the smaller
failure, but it is not a free one.

**Why an escalation and not a resolution.** The schema cannot express "the source assessed a
factor this pack does not have", and there is no field in which to record an assessed level
against a factor label the pack does not carry. This entry is to be amended, not replaced, if a
7009A pack or a published 7009A→7009B factor concordance later arrives.

## AMB-05 / **ESCALATION ESC-3** — Model risk level has no mechanical source

**Gap.** The workbook requires `Model Risk Level` as "MRL 1–5 per V&V 40 Table 4-1". The source
states the two inputs qualitatively — "high M&S results influence, in the words of the
Standard. The Project also found that the decision held high consequence" (p.11) — together
with a criticality assessment (p.11: single point failure, ~1/300 probability of catastrophic
failure, probable loss of aircraft with significant likelihood of pilot loss). V&V 40 Table 4-1,
which converts influence × consequence onto 1–5, is not in the source and is outside the
evidence boundary.

**Resolution.** Declined; the cell is empty. The extractor's "MRL 3" was corrected out.

**Consequence, stated per A-10.** Three weakener patterns are silenced because they are
conditioned on `modelRiskLevel`: **W-EP-04** (unassessed factor at MRL > 2), **W-NASA-01**
(data pedigree unassessed at MRL > 1) and **W-NASA-04** (use history unassessed at MRL > 2).
Seventeen unassessed factors and a source that describes a potentially fatal failure mode
therefore draw no risk-conditioned firing at all. `modelRiskLevel` is also mandatory for
ProfileComplete, so the declination is one of the reasons the package earns only Minimal
(AMB-11).

**Rule applied.** A-10: decline rather than invent; disclose the declination and its
consequence in the encoding.

## AMB-06 — Contradiction: how many reviewers

**Reading A (p.10, [M&S 36] response):** "Independent reviews performed by three statistical
modelers and more than three engineering practitioners."
**Reading B (p.24, worksheet Technical Review, [M&S 36] row):** "Statistical analysis, model and
findings due to analysis reviewed by **two** NASA statisticians… Test performance, data, model
and findings reviewed by team and independently by engineers."

**Resolution.** Neither reading is preferred. Both are quoted in the description of the
`Independent technical review of analysis, model and findings` evidence row, with this entry
cited. Nothing in the package turns on the count.

**Rule applied.** A-9: record the reading chosen and enter the contradiction with an anchor for
each reading; never harmonize silently. Here the reading chosen is "both, quoted".

## AMB-07 — Contradiction: an approved waiver and no waiver at all

**Reading A (p.6, PREDECLARATIONS ¶3):** "Verification of the analysis code **was waived** since
modeling required relatively straightforward multiple linear regression analysis…"
**Reading B (p.8, [M&S 32](7)):** "Validation using RWS or independent data not required per
investigation team, approved by Technical Authority. **No waivers were required.**" — a single
response that both describes a Technical-Authority-approved dispensation and denies that any
waiver was needed.
**Reading C (p.23, worksheet Caveats, [M&S 32](7) row):** "Waivers to requirements — **None**."

**Resolution.** All three are recorded: A in the rationale of the `Numerical code verification`
factor row, B and C beside it and in the Decision rationale. The package asserts no waiver flag
anywhere, because the field the pack offers for it does not exist and because the source's own
answer is self-contradictory. A-9's tie-break ("the answer outranks the declination") settles
the *validation* half of Reading B — the dispensation described is an answer and "no waivers
were required" is a declination — but it does not settle Reading A against Reading C, both of
which are answers. That residue is **author judgment and remains open.**

**Note on the mechanical check.** The A-7 check that fires when required equals achieved on
every factor is released by a recorded waiver. It is released here by Reading A, quoted in the
row it concerns (`Numerical code verification`, the analysis-code verification that was waived).
That is where the waiver belongs; it was not placed on either populated factor.

## AMB-08 — Over-determination: two source factors point at one pack factor

**Ambiguity.** The pack factor `Model inputs` is answered by two different source factors:
`Input Pedigree` (required 3, achieved 3; p.7, p.25 "Data from controlled test… measurement
system accuracy and precision shown to have inconsequential impact on results") and the input
half of `Validation` (required 1, achieved 1). The source gives no rule for combining them, and
they differ by two levels.

**Resolution.** Declined; no level populated; both source factors named in the row's rationale
and anchor. Folded into ESC-1.

**Rule applied.** A-9 (over-determination) and A-10 (decline rather than invent).

## AMB-09 — The radar figure was not used as a source of numbers

**Ambiguity.** pp. 9–10 carry a star/radar glyph plotting required (blue) against achieved
credibility for all eight factors. It is a second statement of the same values, at figure
precision.

**Resolution.** No value was read off the figure. The figure is used only as a *corroboration*
of the shading recovery: its title, "Credibility Meets or Exceeds Requirements", is inconsistent
with any recovered required level exceeding its achieved level, and none does
(`SHADING_RECOVERY.md`, corroboration 3).

**Rule applied.** A-8: where a value is recoverable only by non-textual means, name the method.
Reading eight polygon vertices off a bitmap glyph is not a method that reproduces, so it was not
used to produce values.

## AMB-10 — Level scales

**Ambiguity.** The source scores on 0–4 ("A lower level 0 indicates insufficient evidence to
make a determination", p.7). The pack uses 0–4 for its six NASA-only factors and 1–5 for its 13
V&V 40 factors.

**Resolution.** Both populated factors (`Data pedigree`, `Results robustness`) are NASA-only
factors on the pack's 0–4 scale, so the levels transfer with no rescaling. No 0–4 value was
ever written onto a 1–5 factor. Residual risk, recorded rather than resolved: identical labels
and identical scales across two revisions of a standard do not guarantee identical *level
descriptors*, and 7009B's descriptors are outside the boundary. The acceptance-criteria cell of
each populated row therefore quotes 7009A's own descriptor text, so a reader can see which
rubric the number was scored against.

## AMB-11 — Profile: left blank, derived, earned

**Ambiguity.** The workbook asks for Minimal or Complete. The source declares no such thing.

**Resolution.** The cell is left empty (source-absent). The importer defaults to Minimal and
then **derives** the profile from package content; the package declares
`ProfileMinimal`, read out of the package rather than off the console. Complete is unreachable
because `modelRiskLevel` was declined (AMB-05) and would also require an assurance level the
source does not state.

**Consequence.** At Minimal the importer does not write `assuranceLevel`, `criteriaSet`,
`deviceClass`, `couName`, `hasUncertaintyQuantification` or the derived credibility metrics.
See AMB-12.

**Rule applied.** A-13: the declared profile must be earned rather than asserted.

## AMB-12 — The source's UQ is quantified but the package does not carry the UofA-level flag

**Ambiguity.** The source gives a quantitative results-uncertainty estimate ([M&S 33](1), p.9:
residual standard deviation 0.0084 cm). The workbook's `Has UQ?` cell records **Yes**, but the
importer writes `hasUncertaintyQuantification` at UofA level only for ProfileComplete, which
this package does not earn (AMB-11).

**Resolution.** The workbook keeps "Yes" (it is what the source says); the package carries the
UQ instead on the evidence node that reports it (`hasUncertaintyQuantification: true`,
`uqMethod`, `metricValue` on the output-comparison result). The UofA-level flag is absent, so
W-AL-02 (UQ present, no sensitivity analysis) cannot fire and W-NASA-05 could not have fired.
A reader who looks only at the UofA node will not see that this source quantifies its
uncertainty.

## AMB-13 — Who the assessor is

**Ambiguity.** K.L. Johnson (NASA NESC) is the author of the published document (p.1 byline).
The modeller inside the worked example is never named: p.24 gives only qualifications ("PhD in
statistics and mathematics… 22 years' experience with NASA").

**Resolution.** `Assessor Name` records Johnson with the role stated ("author of the published
worked example") and the fact that the example's modeller is unnamed. The importer records this
as `statedAssessor` (an extracted fact) and keeps it distinct from `wasAttributedTo`, which is
the operator of this encoding run.

## AMB-14 — The NTRS identifier is not in the document

**Ambiguity.** The document text carries no DOI, report number or URI. "NTRS-20200002832" comes
from the **file name supplied with the task**, not from any admitted passage.

**Resolution.** Recorded, and recorded as such: the workbook anchor for the Source Document cell
says the number comes from the file name. The cell itself holds an IRI minted under this
encoding's namespace (`…/source/ntrs-20200002832-johnson-2020`), because a bare citation string
is dropped from the RDF graph as a non-well-formed subject and the provenance link would then
be invisible. The full citation lives in `SOURCE_SCOPING.md` §1 and in the workbook anchor.

## AMB-15 — Departure from A-3: the documentation-site commit is not pinned

**Gap.** A-3 requires the documentation-site commit current on the day of the run. Outbound
HTTPS to uofa.net returns 403 through this environment's proxy, so no commit could be read.

**Resolution.** Not pinned, and said so in `RUN_LOG.md` §2 rather than left blank or guessed.
A departure from the procedure, recorded here per A-13.

## AMB-16 — Departure from A-3: no repository head to pin

**Gap.** A-3 asks for "your repository or tool version". There is no git checkout in this
environment — the CLI is an installed wheel — so no commit SHA exists to record.

**Resolution.** `uofa-cli 0.11.0` is recorded as the whole of what can be pinned, together with
the pack version and the prompt hash. Recorded as a departure per A-13.

## AMB-17 / **ESCALATION ESC-4** — The importer writes fields the source does not support

**Gap.** Three values appear in the package that no admitted passage supports and that the
workbook offers no way to decline:

1. `reviewType: "internal"` on both ReviewActivity nodes. The source describes these reviews as
   **independent** ("Independent reviews performed by…", p.10; "reviewed by team and
   independently by engineers", p.24). "internal" is an importer default for a SHACL-required
   field.
2. `reviewer: <…/org/reviewer>` on both ReviewActivity nodes — a synthesized IRI, generated
   because the "Compares To" column was correctly left empty (a review activity has no
   comparator).
3. `wasGeneratedBy: <…/activity>` on all five evidence nodes. The importer generates these so
   that W-EP-02 does not fire on every imported result; the source describes no such activity
   entities.

**Why an escalation.** These are assertions in the package's own voice that were not read from
the source and cannot be turned off from the workbook. Working around them (for example by
writing false "Compares To" values to steer the defaults) would be worse. Recorded, not
resolved. Consequence: **W-EP-02 cannot fire on this package**, and its silence must not be read
as the source having documented generation activities for its evidence.

## AMB-18 — Departure from A-2: the minting namespace is not one the encoder controls

**Gap.** A-2 requires a namespace the encoder controls. This encoding was performed by an
automated assistant with no domain of its own, and the author's namespace was not supplied.

**Resolution.** Identifiers are minted under `https://reference-encodings.example.net/uofa`, a
reserved documentation domain (RFC 2606) chosen so it cannot collide with a real namespace.
Because `--base-uri` was passed explicitly, `uofa import` prints no placeholder-domain warning;
that silence does not mean A-2 is satisfied. **Pre-signing blocker:** the package must be
re-imported under a namespace the author controls before it is signed, since the identifier is
covered by the signature and cannot be corrected afterwards.

## AMB-19 — Contradiction: validation both not performed and performed by other means

**Reading A (p.6, PREDECLARATIONS):** "Validation will not be performed." (p.19: "No model
confirmation/ validation using independent data planned or performed.")
**Reading B (p.25, final credibility assessment, Validation row):** "1. No validation runs
planned. RWS data not available. **Validation by visual analysis of test data vs model
expectation.** Problem statement clear; model describes test data well…" — and the factor is
scored 1, not 0, against a predeclared requirement of 1.

**Resolution.** Both recorded; not harmonized. Nothing in the package turns on it, because the
validation-family factors are declined under ESC-1 and carry no level. Reading A is quoted in
the Requirement entity's description; Reading B is quoted in the `Output comparison` row's
rationale.

## AMB-20 / **ESCALATION ESC-2** — No evidence class for a sensitivity analysis

**Gap.** The source documents its sensitivities ([M&S 30], p.22: "Penetration depth is sensitive
to both particle velocity and orientation at impact"; p.25 Results Robustness: "Sensitivities
captured in quantitative model, including for combination of factors (interaction)"). The pack's
evidence-type vocabulary is `ValidationResult | ReviewActivity | ProcessAttestation |
DeploymentRecord | InputPedigreeLink`. There is no SensitivityAnalysis class, and
`hasSensitivityAnalysis` cannot be written from a workbook at all.

**Resolution.** Declined: no evidence node was created for the sensitivity findings, and the
`Results robustness` factor's Linked Evidence cell is empty. Typing them as a ValidationResult
to silence the rule would misdescribe them.

**Consequence.** **W-NASA-06** fires ("Results robustness factor is assessed but has no linked
SensitivityAnalysis evidence") and is dispositioned Accepted: it is true of the package. It is
false of the source, which documents its sensitivities. That difference is this entry.

## AMB-21 — A process attestation the source supports was not created

**Ambiguity.** p.25 rates M&S Process/Product Management 4 on "Standard formal experimental
design and data analysis process rigorously followed and documented in standard form… All review
comments addressed", and p.10 records configuration control and archiving. The pack has a
`ProcessAttestation` evidence class that would fit.

**Resolution.** Not created. The factor it would support is declined under ESC-1, so the
attestation would hang off nothing, and the source describes the process rather than attesting
to it in a form the class expects (`processType`, `attestedBy` are importer defaults — see
ESC-4). Recorded so that the absence is visible as a choice rather than an oversight; a named
reviewer may reverse it.

## AMB-22 / **ESCALATION ESC-5** — The context of use loses its boundary in transit

**Gap.** The source states the boundary of validity of its model in several places: permissible
use ("Model specific to this tire and inflation system design. Model may not apply to
redesigned inflation system and will not apply to any future tire redesign", p.19 [M&S 14]),
the domain of verification (p.18 [M&S 16]), the domain of validation (p.19 [M&S 18]), the
operating envelope of the RWS (temperature/humidity controlled to 50 degC / 65 % RH max, p.14)

The encoding is complete as far as an automated run can take it. Here is what I produced and where.

## Deliverables (all in `work/`)

| File | Step | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `SOURCE_SCOPING.md` | A-1 | 12-item evidence inventory; explicit **admitted / excluded / not-admissible** boundary (the source is half worked example, half 7009A tutorial, in one voice) |
| `AMBIGUITY_LOG.md` | A-1, A-9 | 22 entries, **5 ESCALATIONs** (factor-vocabulary gap, no SensitivityAnalysis class, model-risk-level, importer-written fields, COU boundary), 3 recorded contradictions with an anchor per reading |
| `RUN_LOG.md` | A-2/3/4/11/13 | Lineage (`anthropic` / `claude-sonnet-5`, prompt sha256 `c47bf17…`), pins, what the extractor returned, import + provenance counts, completion statement |
| `raw-extract/johnson-2020-nasa7009.raw.xlsx` | A-4 | Extractor output, untouched (sha256 `91b351f…`) |
| `johnson-2020-nasa7009.xlsx` | A-5/6/7 | Reviewed workbook; `Source Anchor` on all five data sheets; 29 anchored rows |
| `build_workbook.py` | A-6 | How the reviewed workbook was derived from the raw extract |
| `shading_recovery.py`, `shading_recovery_output.txt`, `SHADING_RECOVERY.md` | A-8 | Reproducible recovery of the 8 predeclared levels from green cell fill on p.7, plus 4 corroborations the recovery did not use |
| `REVIEW_LEDGER.md` | A-6 | Cell-by-cell confirm/correct/source-absent/add, with an unfilled **Human** column |
| `johnson-2020-nasa7009.jsonld` | A-11 | **Unsigned** package, `ProfileMinimal` (derived), SHACL conforms, `--protocol-check` 8/8, exit 0 |
| `rules-report.txt`, `rules-firings.json`, `DISPOSITIONS_DRAFT.md` | A-12 | 9 firings / 4 patterns; dispositions for all 9 firings, all 19 expected factors, and the 15 silent patterns |

## The substantive results

- **Required levels existed only as cell shading** (p.7). Recovered by fill geometry: Data Pedigree 3, Verification 3, Validation 1, Input Pedigree 3, Uncertainty Characterization 4, Results Robustness 4, M&S History 3, Process/Product Mgmt 2. Achieved levels come from prose (p.25). Confirmed separately per A-7.
- **The pack's factor vocabulary does not fit the source's** (7009A's 8 factors vs the pack's 19 7009B/V&V-40 factors). Only two labels are shared, so only `Data pedigree` (3/3) and `Results robustness` (4/4) are populated; the other six source factors are declined (ESC-1). **Cost, stated in the encoding:** both of the source's exceedances (Verification 3→4, Process/Product Mgmt 2→4) fall on declined factors and are invisible in the package.
- **Model risk level declined** (ESC-3), which silences `W-EP-04`, `W-NASA-01`, `W-NASA-04` and puts ProfileComplete out of reach.
- The extractor returned nothing for the two factors the package ends up carrying, and set required = achieved on all 11 pairs it did return; every level it produced was corrected out.

## Things the document does not answer — flagged rather than guessed

1. **A-2 namespace:** I control no domain and none was supplied. Identifiers are minted under `https://reference-encodings.example.net/uofa` (RFC 2606 reserved). `uofa import` prints no warning only because `--base-uri` was passed — that silence is not compliance. **Pre-signing blocker** (AMB-18).
2. **A-3 documentation-site commit:** uofa.net returns 403 through this environment's proxy; not pinned (AMB-15). There is no git checkout, so no repo head SHA exists — only `uofa-cli 0.11.0` (AMB-16).
3. **Action classes (Part B):** the protocol names only the endpoints of the controlled set, which is not committed anywhere I can read, so no action class was assigned.
4. **Part B's Not Applicable condition for the alignment family** is stated at package level; I applied it at node level for two `W-AL-01` firings on `ReviewActivity` nodes, flagged in the dispositions table with Accepted as the fallback.
5. **A-6 has not happened.** Every value was machine-drafted and machine-checked against the source. Under A-13 that is preparation; the ledger's Human column is deliberately empty, and the package must not be signed until a named person walks it.
